newsitem.title: DUBAI: Kurdish leader hopes talks will herald peace.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish leader hopes talks will herald peace.

text.p: Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) leader Jalal Talabani has said he hopes planned U.S.-brokered peace talks with the rival Kurdish Democratic Party (KDP) will herald peace in northern Iraq.
"We hope that this meeting will be held on time as scheduled between the PUK and the KDP representatives," Talabani told Iranian radio on Monday.

"We hope it will succeed in consolidating and strengthening the truce and the ceasefire all over Iraqi Kurdistan and also in beginning the peace process so as to achieve national reconciliation...," he said in the interview, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

"There are complicated detailed issues and no one can foretell what will happen before the negotiations start. Let us first see the negotiations start and then see what the U.S., Turkish and British roles will be and then we can judge how things are going."

A U.S.-brokered ceasefire last week halted two months of fighting between the PUK and KDP. Representatives from both groups are due to meet in Ankara this week for peace talks chaired by senior U.S. diplomat Robert Pelletreau.
Diplomats say the KDP's military alliance with Baghdad and its charges that Talabani receives military backing from Iran will be contentious issues at the negotiations.
Iran has repeatedly denied helping Talabani and has called for an end to fighting.
